title: Descent of invariant opens together with compatible morphisms along an etale atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Z$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $p:h_V\to X$ be a representable surjective etale morphism from an $S$-scheme $V$. Let $R=V\times_XV$ be the scheme representing the sheaf fibre product, with projections $s,t:R\to V$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $O\subseteq V$ is an open subscheme such that $s^{-1}(O)=t^{-1}(O)=R_O$, and suppose $q:h_O\to Z$ satisfies $q\circ h_{s|_{R_O}}=q\circ h_{t|_{R_O}}$. There is a unique open subspace $U\subseteq X$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] with $h_V\times_XU=h_O$, and a unique morphism $r:U\to Z$ with $r\circ p|_O=q$. For every $S$-scheme $B$ and $a:h_B\to X$, the fibre product $h_B\times_XU$ is represented by the unique open subscheme $B_O\subseteq B$ whose inverse image under the surjective etale scheme morphism $B\times_XV\to B$ is the inverse image of $O$ under $B\times_XV\to V$. If $a$ factors through $U$, the pullback of $r\circ a$ to this cover equals the pullback of $q$. These descriptions commute with maps of scheme tests and characterize $r$ as a natural transformation. Pullback along $p|_O:h_O\to U$ detects equality of morphisms $U\to Z$. In particular, if $X,Z$ are over an $S$-scheme $T$ and $q$ is over $T$, then $r$ is over $T$. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, or affineness of $R$ is assumed.

proof.text: For every representing pullback of p along a scheme test, transport the etale and surjective projections provided separately by IsEtale and IsSurjective along the canonical Yoneda isomorphism between the representing schemes. The projection is therefore a single fppf cover. Its generated singleton sieve lies in the over topology. The pullback square then shows that p is locally surjective.

Let i=h_O to h_V, f=i followed by p, A=range(f), and G=A.sheafify for the fppf topology. Use Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify_isSheaf for the sheaf condition. First prove A.preimage(p)=range(i): a pair of sections with the same p-image lifts to R by its pullback universal property; invariance of O forces both projections into O, and the open immersion lifting property supplies the required factorization. Sheafification of subfunctors commutes with preimage, directly by naturality and equality of the membership sieves. Since i is monic and h_O is a sheaf by subcanonicity, its range is already a sheaf. Thus G.preimage(p)=range(i). The canonical factor pO:h_O to G gives a pullback square, proved from this equality.

Apply fppf_local_open_subfunctor_descent to X, the explicit sheaf G, its sectionwise injective inclusion, locally surjective p, and the pullback isomorphism just constructed. Its representing open W(B,a) and isomorphism e(B,a) give G.preimage(a)=range(h_inclusion_W) and representability of G into X by open immersions. Thus U=(G,representability) is an OpenSubspace.

For uniqueness of U, prove that a representable subfunctor of a sheaf is a sheaf. On a test section its representing monomorphism of schemes has local sections on the membership sieve. Subcanonicity glues those sections; monicity proves compatibility and identifies the glued composite with the identity. Therefore the original section belongs to the subfunctor. Locally surjective p detects equality of sheaf subfunctors: pull back a section to the image sieve of p, use equality of the preimages, and glue membership in the second subsheaf. This applies to every competing open subspace.

The compatibility of q on R implies it is constant on every sectionwise fibre of f, by the pullback universal property for R. Define a natural map d:range(f) to Z by choosing a preimage of each element; fibrewise compatibility proves independence and naturality. Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafifyLift extends d to r:G to Z and to_sheafifyLift gives pO followed by r=q. The range factor is sectionwise surjective; cancel it and apply to_sheafify_lift_unique to prove detection of equality for maps to every sheaf, hence uniqueness of r.

For a chosen test pullback E, pull G.preimage(a)=h_W back along e. The pullback commutativity and G.preimage(p)=h_O identify its range with h_(v inverse O); open factorization proves the elementary preimage formula for ranges of open inclusions, and equality of these ranges implies equality of their opens. Surjectivity of e makes inverse image injective, giving uniqueness of W. The same preimage formula proves compatibility under every base change. For a test factoring through U, its v-section lies in G.preimage(p)=h_O; choose its open factor w and cancel the monic G-inclusion to identify the two maps into G. Composing with r gives the coverwise formula.

Apply the detection argument to any algebraic-space target Z prime. For the relative-base conclusion use the representable sheaf h_T, a sheaf by subcanonicity, and compare r followed by z with the inclusion followed by x after pO. The assumed equality for q identifies them.

The item, its citer lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map and the cited lem-trf-fppf-local-open-subfunctor-descent are not on route-pivot-dropped.txt (live or side-live). There is no repair note or re-split note and no SGA citation. Step 1: the atlas pullback E_a=B×_X V→B is a single surjective etale cover, hence fppf, with no quasi-compactness needed. Step 2: the local-lift subfunctor G is a sheaf by covering composition and pullback plus the sheaf property of X. Step 3: h_V×_X G=h_O, because invariance s^{-1}O=t^{-1}O pushes the lifts through R into O and open immersions are monomorphisms. Step 4: every hypothesis of the cited lemma (F, G sheaves, α injective, local lifts, cartesian open h_W≅h_U×_F G) is checked, and its conclusions (unique W_{T,a}, cover independence, base change, open-immersion representability) give the B_O clause exactly. Step 5: uniqueness of U by two-sided inclusion of subfunctors through gluing in U'. Steps 6–7: r is glued on the single cover E_a, with the double overlap mapping to R_O; naturality comes from separatedness of Z, and r∘p|_O=q from the pair (v∘e_a,w_a). Step 8: detection via the injectivity half of the equalizer condition, with Z'=h_T for the relative clause. Stacks 03BZ (spaces-properties.tex:473) and 0D2Z (spaces-divisors.tex:2797) were checked in place; proof_origin=agent is honest. Edge cases O=∅, O=V, p=id and Z=∅ all behave as stated. = r) ∧ (∀ (B : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj B ⟶ X.obj.obj) (E : Over S) (e : E ⟶ B) (v : E ⟶ V), IsPullback (yoneda.map v) (yoneda.map e) p a → ∃ W : B.left.Opens, e.left ⁻¹ᵁ W = v.left ⁻¹ᵁ O ∧ (∀ W' : V O = v ∧ yoneda.map e ≫ b ≫ r = yoneda.map w ≫ q) ∧ (∀ (Z' : AlgebraicSpace S) (r₁ r₂ : U.val.toFunctor ⟶ Z'.obj.obj), pO ≫ r₁ = pO ≫ r₂ → r₁ = r₂) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (x : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (z
